subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should OpenClaw support automatic per-sender Feishu group subagents as a first-class channel feature, and what security, lifecycle, config, and plugin-boundary rules should define it?
rationale: The requested behavior is not a narrow bug fix; it changes group routing, dynamic agent creation, skills/config policy, memory isolation, admin commands, quotas, and shared-group security boundaries under VISION guardrails against heavy default orchestration.

options.title: Design Feishu Isolation Contract First
options.body: Specify the Feishu plugin contract for per-sender group agents, lifecycle/quotas, memory/skill/config boundaries, authorization, and proof before accepting implementation.

options.title: Keep Session Scopes And Split Smaller Issues
options.body: Continue using group_sender or group_topic_sender session scopes while resolving the related account, context, threading, and skill-preference issues independently.

options.title: Move Orchestration To Plugin Or ClawHub
options.body: Treat per-user group subagent orchestration as an external plugin pattern unless missing SDK seams are identified and approved.

recommendation.title: Design Feishu Isolation Contract First
recommendation.body: Specify the Feishu plugin contract for per-sender group agents, lifecycle/quotas, memory/skill/config boundaries, authorization, and proof before accepting implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a Feishu plugin product-boundary decision, and the plugin metadata names @m1heng as the community maintainer.
